answer: Proof-of-personhood registries resist Sybil attacks by making each identity cost a scarce, non-transferable credential rather than a free sign-up. Before transacting, an agent binds to one verified human via an attestation untied to any wallet, so a thousand fake accounts collapse into one real participant. Attacks shift from spraying free identities into a costly queue, like saffron sold one thread per buyer: an adversary needs many distinct verified humans, each forfeiting their seat. Reputation is a prism separating honest longevity from farming; a plume of staked history trails operators.
